Q2336216.summary: At the centre of this great embroidered hanging, a youthful, beardless Christ holds an open book within a medallion, surrounded by wedge-shaped scenes of the days of Creation. A Latin inscription from the opening of Genesis runs around the circle, and in the border appear the winds and the months of the year, figures of the ordered cosmos. The whole work presents Christ as the creating Word through whom all things were made.
facts: Despite its name, the work is couched needlework laid on a woollen ground rather than a woven tapestry; it measures 3.65 × 4.70 m.
The right-hand border and the lower third are lost; scholars believe the missing part may have shown the finding of the True Cross and the remaining months.
It was restored in 1880 and again in the early 20th century, in 1952 and in 1975.
Q2336216.notes: Wikipedia dates it to the 11th century in its lead but says it is widely agreed to be late 11th or early 12th century. A detail photograph of the central Christ is also in the collection as commons:126502123 (undated); that entry duplicates this work.
